Also, the addition of banana pepper pickling juice adds a fun kick to classic hummus. My recipe:

  • 2 x 15.5 ounce cans of chickpeas (strain, but keep the juice)
  • Handful of parsley
  • 5 or 6 medium to large cloves of garlic
  • Reserve chickpea juice
  • 1/2 cup tahini
  • 1/2-3/4 cup lemon juice
  • Hot sauce (I use chalula) *pepperoncini or banana pepper juice
  • Kosher salt
  • Cracked pepper

Pulse the garlic cloves and parsley in food processor. Add the chickpeas, pulse. Give a little spatula love to the bowl and keep pulsing. Don't worry if it doesn't seem to be mixing much at this point, that is normal. After the beans are roughly chopped up, put in the half cup of tahini (warning: sticky), the 1/2 cup of lemon juice, the kosher salt (you'll add more later, tis to your taste), and some cracked pepper. Process until it starts looking creamy. Does it need more spatula love? Give it a little to get off the walls. Take a moment and give yourself a taste. Yummy? It will undoubtedly need more lemon, so add that to taste, as well as any salt or pepper. Here, it is all about consistency; add the reserved bean choice until it starts to get creamy. If you are eating immediately, you might want to leave the consistency a bit stiff. But if you are smartly prepping ahead and plan to refrigerate, then add liquid until you think it looks almost too creamy and trust in that it will firm up in the fridge. Last, but not least, give it a kick; add in the hot sauce. Sprinkle it in while processing. Love it. Secret ingredient? Hells yes. If you have any jars of pepperoncinis laying around, I like to add in a bit of the liquid from the jar while I am working with the consistency. BOOM.
